demonstrates: Built a composition measurement harness whose own controls caught a leakage artifact that read in the direction the design wanted, established that naive compartment composition ceilings at two, and then measured a training recipe that lifts four-compartment retention from -45.4% to +44.6%.

claims.section: The run caught two of its own artifacts
claims.note: The first roster's eight-compartment retention. Quoted BECAUSE it was wrong: it is the artifact the cross-gain control caught, not a result.

claims.section: The run caught two of its own artifacts
claims.note: Cross-gain of one foreign compartment scored alone on the primary's held-out text -- the evidence that the +27% was shared vocabulary rather than composition.

claims.section: The run caught two of its own artifacts
claims.note: The larger of the two cross-gains, from the corpus sharing most vocabulary with the primary.

claims.section: The run caught two of its own artifacts
claims.note: Eight-compartment retention on the clean roster, after the leaking corpora were removed. The real number the +27% was hiding.

claims.section: What this binds, and the way past it, which has since been measured
claims.note: Four-compartment retention under naive training, fixed-slot policy. The baseline, and negative.

claims.section: What this binds, and the way past it, which has since been measured
claims.note: Four-compartment retention under the trained-p0.5 composition-aware recipe, measured the following day. Full grid and dose curve are on model-trainer-companioned-training-recipe.
